land.text: 'the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla' claimed by Sargon

successors.note: Who burned palace G c. 2300 is disputed: Sargon (Matthiae, Bryce), Mari in revenge for Terqa (Archi, Biga), a natural fire c. 2290 (Astour). Ebla's second kingdom (c. 2300–2000) and third (c. 2000–1600, a vassal of Yamhad, destroyed by Mursili I c. 1600) need their own dossiers.

capitals.name: Ebla (Tell Mardikh)
capitals.note: 'about 55 km southwest of Aleppo', Idlib Governorate; 'Built c. 3500 BC'.

correction.text: Ebla in Mardikh IIA (c. 3000–2400 BC): the city and its hinterland

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Ebla. Infobox 'First kingdom: c. 3000 BC–c. 2300 BC'. The radius is this dossier's: the page describes no early border. Toward the end of the phase Mari's king Sa'umu 'conquered many Eblaite cities'.

correction.text: 'At its greatest extent, Ebla controlled an area roughly half the size of modern Syria', from Ursa'um in the north to the Damascus area in the south, from Phoenicia and the coastal mountains in the west to Haddu in the east; vassals Emar, Burman, Armi and Halabitu, treaty partner Abarsal, ally Nagar

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the archive period (Igrish-Halam, Irkab-Damu c. 2340, Isar-Damu). Six western governorates approximate 'half the size of modern Syria' without the Euphrates valley (Mari's) and the south; the vassals are drawn in the full colour for want of borders. Soft.

ledger.note: 3000 BCE: the first kingdom of Ebla. Infobox 'c. 3000 BC–c. 2300 BC' for the first kingdom; the city was 'Built c. 3500 BC'; the Early Dynastic page lists Ebla among the states 'to the north and west' with Kish, Mari and Nagar.

region.text: the Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates (Emar and its neighbours), which Iblul-Il of Mari invaded

ledger.note: 2450 BCE: the Ebla–Mari war. Mari's king Sa'umu 'conquered many Eblaite cities'; 'Kun-Damu defeated Mari in the mid-25th century BC'; later Ebla 'paid tribute to Mari under Igrish-Halam' and 'the Mariote king Iblul-Il invaded Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates'. Start year bridged to Kun-Damu's victory; Mari 'fought many wars against Ebla during the 24th century BC' (Early Dynastic page).

region.text: 'roughly half the size of modern Syria', from Ursa'um to the Damascus area, from Phoenicia and the coastal mountains to Haddu

ledger.note: 2400 BCE: Ebla at its greatest extent. The page gives the extent without a date; -2400 is the start of the archive phase (Mardikh IIB1) that follows IIA (c. 3000–2400). Bridged.

2300 BCE: the war ends with Ebla's destruction. Under Isar-Damu the vizier Ibbi-Sipish 'won a battle near Terqa' (undated); 'the first destruction' of palace G is dated c. 2300 BC, by Mari 'in revenge for Terqa, about three or four years after the battle' (Archi and Biga) or by Sargon.

2300 BCE: palace G burns and the first kingdom ends. 'the first destruction to c. 2300 BC'; Matthiae and Bryce blame Sargon of Akkad ('the Upper Land: Mari, Iarmuti, and Ebla'), Archi and Biga Mari, Astour 'a natural fire, dated c. 2290 BC'; Pettinato once dated it c. 2500/2400 and blamed Eannatum or Lugalzagesi. The counterpart follows Sargon's claim; Ebla's second kingdom (c. 2300–2000) rose on the same site.

wars.name: Ebla–Mari war

zones.text: the Eblaite cities on the middle Euphrates

wars.outcome: Sa'umu of Mari took Eblaite cities; Kun-Damu defeated Mari (mid-25th century); Ebla paid tribute under Igrish-Halam while Iblul-Il invaded the middle Euphrates; 'Ebla recovered under Irkab-Damu in about 2340 BC and counter-attacked Mari'; Ibbi-Sipish won near Terqa; palace G burned c. 2300.
wars.note: The Mari page: Ebla's first destruction 'in c. 2300 BC', 'after Mari's war with Ebla, which included a Mariote victory at Terqa' (its wording differs: a Mariote victory, not Ebla's).

certainty.note: 'Half the size of modern Syria' bounded by named towns (Ursa'um, Damascus area, Haddu) and vassal kingdoms; no line is drawn on any page.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks: the first kingdom of Ebla, -3000..-2300. Only the Ebla page carries the extent, undated and in words ('half the size of modern Syria'); it is rendered as six western Syrian governorates from -2400 and as the city alone before. The Ebla–Mari war's start, Ebla's tribute to Mari (recorded in the mari dossier as vassal_start -2360 / vassal_end -2340) and the destroyer of palace G are all bridged at confidence 1; the pages disagree on who won at Terqa. Ebla's second kingdom (c. 2300–2000, destroyed c. 2000, Amar-Sin's year 7 c. 2040 mentions an ensi of Ebla) and third kingdom (c. 2000–1600, vassal of Yamhad, destroyed by Mursili I c. 1600) need dossiers from the Levant group. Ebla resolves in the gazetteer; Emar, Armi, Nagar, Ursa'um do not.
